subject: Washington Monument
title: The Washington Monument's Tip Is a Metal Once Priced Like Silver

scenes.text: The tip of the Washington Monument was once shown off at Tiffany's.
It's a small pyramid, about nine inches tall, weighing one hundred ounces.
Before it went up in 1884, it sat in a New York jewelry store window.
The metal cost about a dollar an ounce, the price of silver, roughly a monument worker's daily pay.
It was aluminum. Then in 1886, a new electric method made it cheap almost overnight.
Today you wrap sandwiches in it. Once, it crowned a monument.

description:
The Washington Monument is capped by a 100-ounce pyramid of solid aluminum, set in place on December 6, 1884. Aluminum then cost about $1.10 an ounce, roughly the price of silver, and the maker displayed the tip at Tiffany's in New York before it was installed.
In 1886 Charles Martin Hall and Paul Héroult found the electrolytic process that made aluminum cheap.
What everyday thing do you think will be a luxury in 100 years?
first_comment: Charles Martin Hall was 22 when he cracked cheap aluminum, and the company that grew from it later became Alcoa. What would you have guessed the tip was made of?
